case_title: Balvir Singh v. State of Madhya Pradesh
accused_occupation: Railway worker (accused No.1 Harnam Singh, per the judgment)
accused_victim_relationship: Co-worker in the railways; prior enmity over money transactions; a quarrel 2-3 days before the incident
statutory_provisions: IPC s.341; IPC s.302 r/w s.34; Arms Act s.25(1A) r/w s.27
evidence_type: Eyewitness (PWs 2, 3, 13); medical (post-mortem, PW-9); recovery of pistol; FSL report
confession: Disclosure/confessional statement of accused No.1 leading to recovery of pistol; recovery relied on as proved by IO (PW-14)
aggravating_circumstances: Close-range shot to the victim's face; victim was held by two accused when shot; victim died instantly
trial_court_outcome: Convicted accused 1-4 under IPC s.341 and s.302 (with s.34 for 2-4); accused 1 also under Arms Act s.25(1A)/27; life imprisonment with fine of Rs.1,000 for accused 1 and for accused 2-3 (fine Rs.1,000 each), one month RI under s.341 for accused 2-4
high_court_outcome: Appeal dismissed; High Court affirmed convictions and life sentences (including Arms Act conviction of accused 1)
offence_finally_established: Accused 1 (Harnam Singh): IPC s.302, IPC s.341, Arms Act s.25(1A) r/w s.27. Accused 2 and 3 acquitted of s.302/34 and s.341
neutral_facts: On a day in March 1998 at about 5.30 pm, the victim was riding a motorcycle with two companions when a group of four men stopped it near a lane. One of the men asked the victim to get down to talk. When the victim got down, one attacker struck the victim on the back with a lathi. The victim ran toward a lane to escape. Two other men allegedly caught hold of the victim's arms, and the accused who had the pistol fired at close range at the victim's face, killing the victim instantly. Three eyewitnesses, two of them the victim's companions on the motorcycle and one nearby, described these acts consistently. The defence alleged no eyewitness was present. The post-mortem found a gunshot wound to the left eye and brain, with gunpowder in the eyes, and nine other injuries on the back, arms, chest and head. The doctor opined that the shot was fired from about one foot away. Following a disclosure, a country-made pistol was recovered from a house. Forensic examination found the pistol operative, but the barrel marks on the bullet were insufficient for decisive matching. The FIR was registered at a police station on the same day at 6 pm, and an inquest was conducted at the scene.
physical_harm: Death by gunshot to the face/left eye (bullet lodged in brain); nine other injuries including bruises, contusion, lacerated and incised wounds from lathi and other blows
number_of_offences: 10 charged (IPC ss.147, 148, 149, 341, 294, 323, 506B, 302; Arms Act s.25 r/w s.27; SC/ST Act s.3(2)(V)); 3 finally upheld (for accused 1: IPC ss.302, 341; Arms Act s.25(1A) r/w s.27)
premeditation_planning: No premeditation or prior meeting of minds found for accused 2 and 3; planning for accused 1 not separately discussed
motive: alleged: enmity arising from money transactions between accused No.1 and the victim, with a quarrel 2-3 days earlier
key_evidence_accepted: Consistent eyewitness testimony of PWs 2, 3 and 13 attributing specific overt acts; post-mortem findings; recovery of pistol proved by IO; FSL report
witness_credibility: Eyewitnesses found credible and trustworthy; contradictions on number of blows, distance and body part were minor errors of observation; Devendra Rai's criminal antecedents did not discredit him
bail_history: Not stated (bail bonds of accused 2 and 3 discharged on their acquittal; no other bail history)
trial_duration: offence: 11.03.1998; trial judgment: not given; High Court: 26.08.2008; Supreme Court: 19.02.2019
legal_representation: Appellants: Raj Kishor Choudhary, Abdul Karim Ansari, Shakeel Ahmed, Chitranjali Negi, Aftab Ali Khan, Sanjay Jain. State: Swarupama Chaturvedi, B. N. Dubey, Mukesh Kumar, Indira Bhakar, Aparna Trivedi, Santanu Singh
investigation_status: FIR registered 11.03.1998; inquest conducted; accused arrested; pistol seized; charge sheet filed; 14 prosecution witnesses examined
procedural_irregularity: None noted by the court; defence alleged FIR was antedated and delayed, rejected by the court
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted accused 1-4 (s.341, s.302/34) and accused 1 under Arms Act; High Court: appeal dismissed, convictions affirmed; Supreme Court: accused 1 conviction affirmed; accused 2 and 3 convictions under s.302/34 and s.341 set aside
prosecution_argument: Eyewitness evidence is corroborated by medical evidence and FSL report; conviction should not be interfered with
defence_argument: Blind murder with no genuine eyewitnesses; FIR antedated; medical evidence contradicts eyewitnesses on weapons and distance; FSL report inconclusive; s.34 wrongly invoked against accused 2 and 3
legal_principle_applied: Minor discrepancies do not discredit credible eyewitnesses; oral evidence has primacy over medical opinion; s.34 requires common intention shown by overt acts and prior meeting of minds
precedent_relied_upon: Appabhai (1988) Suppl. SCC 241; Annareddy Sambasiva Reddy (2009) 12 SCC 546; Rammi alias Rameshwar (1999) 8 SCC 649; Ramanand Yadav (2003) 12 SCC 606; Ramesh Singh alias Phooti (2004) 11 SCC 305; State of U.P. v. Krishna Gopal (1988) 4 SCC 302 (relied on or referred to)
other_sentence_order: Accused 1 (Harnam Singh) to surrender within four weeks to serve remaining sentence; otherwise taken into custody
